messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: warning #44
parts:
Magaly, the 'no adjustment' warning is OK - it just means that Distance
can't assess whether the hazard-rate model without adjustment is an
adequate model. The absence of a chi-square test is the same issue.
With only 3 intervals, if you fit a 2-parameter detection function, you
have no information to assess how good the fit is. Parameter 2
constrained at a lower bound is potentially a bit more of an issue, as
that suggests that your estimated detection function may fall steeply
from the first interval. In that circumstance, different models can
give very different density estimates.

What worries me is that you say you left-truncate your first interval
because of evasive movement - but left-truncation can't deal with
evasive movement! If for example you have too few detections in your
first interval and too many in your second interval because of this
movement, then that would explain why the estimated detection function
falls off steeply from the 2nd to the 3rd interval. If this is what is
happening, you should not left-truncate. Distance will then tend to
average out the lack of animals in the 1st interval with the surplus of
animals in the 2nd interval, and you should then get less biased density
estimates. Of course, the goodness-of-fit test is likely to indicate
that you have a poor fit - but that is due to a problem with the data
more than a problem with the model.

Steve Buckland

Magaly Chambellant wrote:
> > Good Day,
> >
> > I am running CDS to etimate the density of seals on the ice. My data came
> > from an aerial survey (10 lines) and I had to left truncate the first distance
> > interval to account for the evasive response of seals. I am left with 3 intervals
> > of 100m each.
> > the best fitted model according to the AIC is the uniform/cosine. However,
> > visually I think that this model is not biologically sound and that a better
> > model would be the hazard rate. The problem is I get the following warnings
> > when I run the analysis with the hazard rate model:
> >
> > ** Warning: The number of intervals - 1 equals the number of key
> > parameters 2 so no adjustments can be made. **
> > ** Warning: Parameter 2 is at a lower bound. **
> >
> > I understand that Distance cannot make any adjustments but I am not sure I
> > understand the consequences of it. Moreover, no chi-test could be run due, I
> > think, to the number of parameters compared to the number of intervals (i.e.
> > higher). So I am not sure if it would be reasonnable to use the hazard rate
> > model.
> >
> > I would appreciate your insight.
> >
> > Thank you,
> >
> > Magaly
